comment: Shared memory / Knowledge commands, plus the services::* orchestration
enums and settings_writer.
Schema and rules: see 00-foundation.json. One file per domain so the
registry can be appended to in parallel; a duplicate code across two
files is a hard error in the loader.
Two groups live here, and they are not the same kind of thing.
1. owner: "core" — the seven enums that were the last ones still
riding generic {{detail}}-only command codes (accounts.login_failed,
desktop.switch_failed, and friends, all now deleted). Three
distinctions in this group are load-bearing and a translator must
not smooth them over:
account_register.cc_live_refresh_skipped is a REFUSAL, not a
failure. Claudepot declined to spend the single-use refresh
token because a live `claude` session is running and rotating
it would sign that session out. It is strictly transient — the
next pass succeeds. A sentence that reads as a re-login prompt
is actively harmful.
account_register.auth_rejected IS the re-login case, and the only
one. Both the access token and its refresh token were refused.
account_register.cc_changed_during_refresh sits between them:
nothing was lost, retry.
wake.no_credentials / wake.identity_unverified mean NOTHING WAS
BILLED; wake.token / wake.request mean a request may have gone
out. The user's question is "did that cost me anything", and
one shared sentence would answer it wrong half the time.
desktop_clear.data_dir_missing is a success in disguise — Desktop
was already signed out. Keep that framing.
settings_write.contended means another writer (Claude Code, or the
user's editor) kept moving the file while we rebased onto it.
Nothing was written and nothing was lost; the remedy is "try
again", never a repair or a restore.
2. owner: "command" — ad-hoc rejections raised in
src-tauri/src/commands/shared_memory.rs. Their English carries the
internal command label the old frontend regex layer used to strip
("list: ", "counts_by_project: "); the code is what replaces that
guesswork, and `message` keeps the label so the untranslated
fallback still says exactly what it always said.
shared_memory.index_unavailable and shared_memory.excerpt_unavailable
are the two that inherited real remediation copy from the deleted
src/lib/errors.ts regex layer. The first is "restart, or rebuild
from Settings -> Cleanup"; the second is "the transcript moved or
was pruned". excerpt_unavailable is raised only for a locator that
is unknown to the index or whose file is NotFound on disk — a
permission error is shared_memory.read_failed, because telling a
user their transcript is gone when it is merely unreadable would
send them looking for a backup they do not need.
